source_text: Long-term sequelae specific to excision include chronic urinary tract infections from scarred urethral orifices, dyspareunia arising from tissue loss and fibrosis, and obstetric challenges such as prolonged labor and perineal tears, as the removal of labial structures impairs natural vulvar elasticity and lubrication. [17] [3]
